## 1. Purpose

This SOP describes the specifications, assembly, maintenance, and
ordering of replacement parts for the Price Pygmy and Price Type AA
mechanical current meters used by the EA Program. These vertical-axis
cup-type meters convert water velocity into rotational counts and are
the standard instruments for measuring point velocities during stream
discharge measurements (see
[SOP-F42 Stream Discharge Measurement](SOP-F42-stream-discharge-measurement.qmd)).


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Price Pygmy current meters and Price Type AA current
  meters owned by the EA Program, including standard cat-whisker and
  magnetic-head contact chamber variants
- **Does not apply to:** Electronic velocity meters (e.g.,
  Marsh-McBirney, FlowTracker ADV), propeller-type meters (e.g., Ott),
  or acoustic Doppler instruments
- **Location:** Instruments are stored in the EA field equipment room;
  maintenance is performed in SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                         |
|:------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve purchases, authorize meter retirement          |
| Field Lead        | Perform pre-field spin tests, coordinate maintenance   |
| Trained Personnel | Assemble, inspect, and clean meters per this SOP       |
| New Students      | Complete training before handling meters                |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Pivot points and shaft tips are sharp; handle with care.
  The bucket wheel can pinch fingers if spun while adjusting the
  assembly.
- **Chemical:** Instrument oil is a mild skin irritant. Avoid eye
  contact.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when oiling or cleaning with solvents)
- [ ] Safety glasses (when using compressed air for cleaning)


## 5. Instrument Specifications

### 5.1 Price Type AA Current Meter

The Type AA is the standard USGS Price-type current meter for general
streamflow measurement. The bucket wheel has six conical cups, is
5 inches (12.7 cm) in diameter, and rotates on a vertical axis inside
a brass yoke. Tungsten carbide bearings are seated in deeply recessed
inverted cups that trap air and exclude water and silt from the bearing
surfaces. A tailpiece assembly keeps the meter aligned with the current
when suspended by cable.

| Parameter              | Value                                      |
|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Velocity range         | 0.1--25 ft/s (0.03--7.6 m/s)              |
| Bucket wheel diameter  | 5 in (12.7 cm)                             |
| Number of cups         | 6                                          |
| Contact types          | Single revolution and penta (every 5 rev)  |
| Suspension             | Wading rod or cable with sounding weight   |
| Construction           | Brass and stainless steel, chrome plated   |
| Rating                 | USGS standard rating table (two equations joined at 1 rev/s = 2.2 ft/s) |

### 5.2 Price Pygmy Current Meter

The Pygmy meter is scaled to two-fifths the size of the Type AA and is
designed for shallow streams where a full-size meter would occupy too
much of the flow depth. The contact chamber is integral to the yoke and
provides a single-revolution contact only (no penta gear). The meter
has no tailpiece and cannot be used with cable suspension.

| Parameter              | Value                                      |
|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Velocity range         | 0.1--4.9 ft/s (0.03--1.5 m/s)             |
| Bucket wheel diameter  | 2 in (5.1 cm)                              |
| Number of cups         | 6                                          |
| Contact type           | Single revolution only                     |
| Suspension             | Wading rod only (no cable suspension)      |
| Construction           | Brass and stainless steel, chrome plated   |
| Rating                 | USGS standard rating table (single equation) |

### 5.3 Choosing Between Meters

| Condition                                  | Meter to Use |
|:-------------------------------------------|:-------------|
| Water depth > 1.0 ft (0.3 m)              | Type AA      |
| Water depth $\leq$ 1.0 ft (0.3 m)         | Pygmy        |
| Velocities expected > 4.9 ft/s            | Type AA      |
| Shallow stream edges (supplemental data)   | Pygmy        |
| Cable suspension required                  | Type AA      |


## 6. Equipment and Accessories

### 6.1 Meter Components and Accessories

| Item                              | Used With      | Notes                          |
|:----------------------------------|:---------------|:-------------------------------|
| Top-setting wading rod            | Both           | Graduated in tenths of a foot; depth-setting mechanism on handle |
| Round wading rod                  | Both           | Simpler design; depth read from rod markings |
| Headset (earpiece)                | Both           | For counting clicks manually   |
| AquaCalc or digital flow computer | Both           | Automatically counts revolutions and computes velocity |
| Stopwatch                         | Both           | For timed revolution counts if no digital counter |
| Sounding weight (Columbus type)   | Type AA only   | For cable-suspended measurements |
| Tailpiece assembly                | Type AA only   | Remove when using wading rod   |
| Electrical cable                  | Both           | Connects meter to counter or headset |

### 6.2 Maintenance Supplies

| Item                              | Notes                                    |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Instrument oil (light machine oil)| Supplied with meter; for pivot bearings   |
| Lint-free cloth                   | For cleaning and drying                  |
| Cotton swabs (pointed)            | For cleaning pivot bearing recesses      |
| Small flat-head screwdriver       | For contact chamber adjustments          |
| Magnifying glass or loupe         | For inspecting pivot points for burrs    |
| Paper clip                        | For checking pivot magnetization         |
| Bulk magnetic tape eraser         | For demagnetizing pivots                 |
| Soft-bristle brush                | For removing debris from cups            |
| Compressed air (filtered)         | For drying internal components           |


## 7. Procedure

### 7.1 Assembly

**Type AA on a wading rod:**

1. Remove the tailpiece assembly (it is only used for cable suspension)
2. Slide the meter yoke onto the wading rod and secure with the
   thumbscrew
3. Connect the electrical cable from the binding posts on the contact
   chamber to the counter (AquaCalc) or headset
4. If using the penta contact (every 5 revolutions), connect the cable
   to the penta binding post; for single-revolution counting, use the
   single-revolution binding post

**Pygmy on a wading rod:**

1. Slide the pygmy yoke directly onto the wading rod and secure with
   the thumbscrew
2. Connect the electrical cable from the binding post to the counter or
   headset. The pygmy has only a single-revolution contact.

### 7.2 Pre-Field Spin Test

Perform a spin test before every field outing to verify the meter is
functioning properly. Conduct the test with the meter level, the shaft
vertical, and in a location with no air currents.

::: {.callout-important}
Always spin the bucket wheel counterclockwise as viewed from above.
Never spin in the opposite direction -- this can damage the contact
wires and produce inaccurate readings.
:::

1. Hold the meter with the shaft vertical and level (do not set the
   Type AA on its tail fins, as this does not produce a level position)
2. Spin the bucket wheel briskly counterclockwise
3. Time how long the wheel continues to spin freely

| Meter   | Minimum Spin Time | Optimum Spin Time |
|:--------|:------------------|:------------------|
| Type AA | 2 minutes 00 seconds | 3 minutes 30 seconds or more |
| Pygmy   | 1 minute 00 seconds  | 1 minute 30 seconds or more  |

4. If the spin time falls below the minimum, clean and oil the meter
   (see Section 8) and retest
5. Record spin test results on the field data sheet

### 7.3 Post-Field Cleaning

1. Rinse the entire meter thoroughly with clean fresh water immediately
   after use
2. Gently shake excess water from the bucket wheel and yoke
3. Dry all surfaces with a lint-free cloth
4. Apply a small drop of instrument oil to the pivot bearing and the
   upper shaft bearing
5. Store the meter in its carrying case with the raising nut loosened so
   the bucket wheel rests on the pivot without spring tension


## 8. Maintenance

### 8.1 Routine Maintenance (After Every 5--10 Uses)

1. **Clean the pivot bearing.** Remove the bucket wheel assembly by
   loosening the raising nut and lifting the assembly off the pivot.
   Clean the inside of the pivot bearing with a pointed cotton swab.
   A clean bearing will have a visible shine.

2. **Inspect the pivot point.** Examine the pivot under a magnifying
   glass for burrs, rounding, or damage. A pivot with burrs will
   produce inaccurate readings. Replace the pivot if the tip is rounded
   or burred.

3. **Check for magnetization.** Touch the pivot to a paper clip. If the
   pivot lifts the paper clip, it has become magnetized. Demagnetize
   using a bulk magnetic tape eraser.

4. **Oil the bearings.** Apply one small drop of instrument oil to the
   upper shaft bearing and one drop to the pivot. Do not over-oil --
   excess oil attracts grit.

5. **Inspect the bucket wheel.** Spin the wheel slowly and watch for
   wobble in the frame or hub. If the upper portion of the hub wobbles
   more than the lower portion, the shaft is bent and must be replaced.

6. **Inspect the contact chamber.** For cat-whisker contacts, check
   that the wire makes clean contact with the solder bead on each
   revolution. For magnetic-head contacts, verify the counter registers
   properly during the spin test.

::: {.callout-warning}
### Raising Nut Caution
Never loosen the raising nut by holding the nut and spinning the bucket
wheel. This will bend the shaft. Always hold the bucket wheel still and
unscrew the nut.
:::

### 8.2 Annual Maintenance

1. Disassemble the meter completely: remove bucket wheel, shaft, and
   pivot
2. Clean all parts with a lint-free cloth dampened with instrument oil
3. Inspect the shaft for straightness by rolling on a flat surface
4. Replace worn or damaged parts (see Section 9)
5. Reassemble the meter and adjust the pivot per the manufacturer's
   instructions
6. Perform a spin test to verify performance
7. Record maintenance date, parts replaced, and spin test results in
   the instrument log

### 8.3 Pivot Adjustment

Correct pivot adjustment is critical for accurate readings:

1. Hold the meter in an inverted position with the pivot pointing up
2. Release the keeper screw for the pivot-adjusting nut and unscrew a
   few turns
3. Temporarily tighten the set screw and advance the pivot-adjusting
   nut until it touches the yoke
4. Set the pivot end play to approximately 0.001 in -- the shaft should
   have just barely perceptible vertical play, detectable by feel with
   a fingernail or against sensitive skin
5. Tighten the keeper screw to lock the adjustment

### 8.4 Storage

- Store meters in their waterproof carrying cases
- Loosen the raising nut to relieve pressure on the pivot
- Ensure meters are clean and lightly oiled
- Store in a dry location away from dust and vibration
- If a meter will not be used for more than 3 months, remove the bucket
  wheel assembly and store separately


## 9. Ordering Parts and Supplies

### 9.1 Supplier

The primary supplier for USGS-type Price AA and Pygmy current meters
and replacement parts in the United States is:

**Performance Results Plus, Inc.**\
Website: [prph2o.com](https://prph2o.com)\

*TBD -- confirm current contact information and whether Geo Scientific
(geoscientific.ca) is a preferred alternative supplier. Verify current
pricing and lead times.*

### 9.2 Replacement Parts to Stock

Maintain the following spare parts inventory to avoid delays when a
meter fails a spin test:

| Part                              | Quantity to Stock | Fits          |
|:----------------------------------|:------------------|:--------------|
| Pivot (tungsten carbide tip)      | 2                 | Both          |
| Shaft                             | 1 per meter type  | AA or Pygmy   |
| Bucket wheel assembly             | 1 per meter type  | AA or Pygmy   |
| Bucket wheel hub nut              | 2                 | Both          |
| Raising nut                       | 1 per meter type  | AA or Pygmy   |
| Cat-whisker wire and solder bead  | 2 sets            | AA            |
| Instrument oil                    | 1 bottle          | Both          |
| Pivot bearing                     | 2                 | Both          |

::: {.callout-note}
Parts for the Type AA and the BTA (bottom-tracking acoustic) meter are
interchangeable except for the yoke and contact chamber. This means
the lab does not need separate inventories of pivots, shafts, and hub
assemblies for both meter types.
:::

### 9.3 Rating Tables

Each meter ships with a USGS-approved standard rating table that
converts bucket wheel revolutions per second to velocity in ft/s or
m/s. Rating tables are also available for download from the supplier's
website:

- Type AA rating table:
  [English](https://prph2o.com/usgs-type-aa-current-meter/) |
  [Metric](https://prph2o.com/usgs-type-aa-current-meter/)
- Pygmy rating table:
  [English](https://prph2o.com/usgs-pygmy-current-meter/) |
  [Metric](https://prph2o.com/usgs-pygmy-current-meter/)

Keep a laminated copy of the appropriate rating table in each meter's
carrying case and a digital copy on the lab shared drive.

### 9.4 Meter Calibration Verification

USGS studies have found that approximately 35% of Type AA meters and
20% of Pygmy meters in routine field use fail to meet standard rating
criteria, typically because of worn pivots, bent shafts, or damaged
contacts. The spin test (Section 7.2) is the primary field check. If
a meter consistently falls below the optimum spin time even after
cleaning and oiling, it should be repaired or retired.

*TBD -- determine whether the EA Program should establish a periodic
recalibration schedule (e.g., sending meters to a USGS hydrologic
instrumentation facility) or whether spin-test-based screening is
sufficient.*


## 10. Troubleshooting

| Problem                            | Probable Cause                | Corrective Action |
|:-----------------------------------|:------------------------------|:------------------|
| Spin time below minimum            | Dirty or worn pivot; bent shaft; dry bearings | Clean pivot bearing; inspect pivot for burrs; oil bearings; replace pivot or shaft if damaged |
| Counter not registering clicks     | Loose cable connection; worn cat-whisker wire; dead battery in digital counter | Check cable connections; inspect and replace contact wire; replace counter battery |
| Bucket wheel wobbles during spin   | Bent shaft or bent bucket wheel frame | Replace shaft; if hub wobbles, replace bucket wheel assembly |
| Meter reads high compared to known velocity | Magnetized pivot; pivot bearing worn oversize | Demagnetize pivot; replace pivot bearing |
| Meter reads low compared to known velocity | Excessive friction; pivot burr; over-oiled bearings attracting grit | Clean and re-oil; replace pivot if burred |

## 12. Training Record

Before handling or using current meters independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-F01 Field Safety](SOP-F01-field-safety.qmd) training
3. Observe a trained operator assemble, spin-test, and clean both meter
   types
4. Successfully perform assembly and spin test under supervision
5. Read the stream discharge measurement procedure in
   [SOP-F42](SOP-F42-stream-discharge-measurement.qmd) before using
   meters in the field
6. Be signed off by the PI or designated trainer
